| Scene description | • S14-A is in busy Jianghan Road Food Street, with grey stone paving.<br>• S14-A-01 shows tidy wooden classification bins beside the path, lined with black bags and clearly labelled ‘Recyclables’ and ‘Residual waste’, without overflow.<br>• S14-A-02 shows a green food-waste container beside a lane wall, with waste spilling over its top, white bags and paper, and a little ground litter.<br>• S14-A-03 shows transparent foam packaging along a blue barrier and the pavement edge, partly covering an advertising board, with scattered paper.<br>• S14-A-04 shows two black ‘Residual waste’ bins beside the road: the right bag bulges and overflows, while the left bin does not. Scooters stand behind.<br>• S14-A-05 shows an open white ‘Rice noodles’ bag of unidentified waste hanging beside a post, with a few scattered items beneath. |
| Regulatory basis | • Containers should be clean and free of spills, accessible without obstructing pedestrians, and maintained through scheduled collection and daily checks by sanitation operators and subdistrict offices. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 18.<br>• Public-space stockpiling and littering are prohibited; busy areas should have sufficient functioning classification bins. Measures for the Management of Municipal Solid Waste, Article 12.<br>• Overflow or accumulation exceeding two-thirds of container volume requires immediate removal; bags should be tied, without spills, and containers intact and unstained. Standard for the Provision of Urban Environmental Sanitation Facilities, Section 5.2.3.<br>• Checks, reporting, dispatch, correction and feedback should form a traceable management process supported by records. Technical Code for Municipal Solid Waste Collection and Transport, Section 4.3.2.<br>• Delayed collection causing overflow, accumulation or pollution may attract warnings, fines or suspension in serious cases, applicable after three or more consecutive failures to correct or major sanitation risks. Regulations on Urban Appearance and Environmental Sanitation Management, Article 35. |
| Severity | **Moderate.** Two overflow locations and five accumulations, without extensive pollution or strong odours, create visual and potential sanitation risks in a busy food street. Pavement-edge piles also affect safe passage. |
| Impact assessment | Visible effects: spills and scattered items cover ground and an advertising board, impair appearance and create trip risks. Near-term risks: increased humidity in cloudy weather may encourage bacteria and insects; pedestrians may trample and spread waste; delayed clearance may cause complaints or media attention. |
| Potential causes | • Collection may be insufficient after lunch or dinner peaks: S14-A-02 and S14-A-04 overflow, and S14-A-03 packaging may be temporary business storage.<br>• Businesses or residents may misclassify food waste or hang bags improperly: S14-A-05 has an open ‘Rice noodles’ bag with unidentified contents.<br>• Temporary barrier or construction areas may retain packaging or construction waste, as in S14-A-03.<br>• Verify collection records, business classification, recent construction or temporary stalls, and observe peak filling rates and collection response times. |
| Long-term effects | Persistent or recurrent problems could normalise poor sanitation, reduce satisfaction and harm urban appearance. Long-standing accumulation may cause vectors, odours or public-health incidents and weaken confidence and participation in classification. |
| Recommendations | • Immediate action: empty S14-A-02 and S14-A-04, clear S14-A-03 foam and the S14-A-05 hanging bag, sweep scattered items and keep paths unobstructed.<br>• Longer-term action: (1) increase peak-period collection through scheduled and responsive service; (2) educate and supervise businesses, provide classification signs, and discourage or penalise violations; (3) require construction operators to clear their own waste and include barrier areas in checks; (4) link reporting, rapid response and corrective feedback using smart monitoring or public reporting platforms. |
| Priority | **High.** Overflow and accumulation in this busy food street directly affect appearance and pedestrian safety and create sanitation risks. Immediate response is warranted to prevent escalation. |
